summary: Build a networked monitor that reads particulates, CO2, and VOCs and shows them on a live dashboard: a sensor on an ESP32, firmware you describe in YAML, a driver library, an MQTT transport, and a self-hosted dashboard. Software is free/OSS; the sensors are cheap and orderable.

capabilities.query: pm2.5 co2 voc air quality sensor sen55 scd41
adafruit circuitpython pm25 air quality sensor driver

build_steps.title: Wire the sensor to the ESP32
build_steps.detail: Connect the SEN55 (and/or SCD41) to the ESP32 over I2C (SDA/SCL + 3V3 + GND). Confirm the wiring against the board pinout.

build_steps.title: Flash firmware
build_steps.detail: Describe the node in an ESPHome YAML (board + the SEN55/SCD41 sensor component + Wi-Fi), then compile and flash. No C to write. (CircuitPython + the Adafruit driver is the alternative.)

build_steps.title: Publish telemetry
build_steps.detail: Have the node publish readings over MQTT to a Mosquitto broker (ESPHome can also talk to Home Assistant directly).

build_steps.title: Show it on a dashboard
build_steps.detail: Ingest into Home Assistant for cards + history + alerts, or into InfluxDB + Grafana for charts. Set an alert when CO2 or PM2.5 crosses a threshold.
